analysis.investment_thesis: Aakaar Medical trades at a P/E of 11.90 but delivers an anemic ROE of just 0.34%, indicating earnings are essentially trivial relative to equity. Without a proven multi-year earnings record, dividend history, or demonstrable margin of safety, this micro-cap (INR 71.7 Cr) fails nearly every quantitative filter I demand.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 67.05% signals skin in the game
P/E of 11.90 is below my <15 ceiling on headline basis
DII participation of 11.17% offers some institutional validation
key_risks: ROE of 0.34% implies earnings are near-zero — the 'E' in P/E is fragile
Micro-cap at INR 71.7 Cr — illiquid, volatile, no durable earning power demonstrated
Zero FII and no disclosed dividend history or balance-sheet strength metrics
red_flags: 0.34% ROE suggests the low P/E is a statistical artifact of collapsed earnings
Recently listed aesthetic/cosmetics micro-cap — speculative by Graham's IPO test
No data on current ratio, debt/equity, or interest coverage to verify solvency
analysis.detailed_analysis:
A P/E of 11.90 looks superficially cheap, but pair it with an ROE of 0.34% and the math tells the real story: earnings are nominal, making the multiple meaningless. On a rough back-of-envelope basis, if ROE is 0.34%, book value per share must be enormous relative to EPS — or EPS is near zero — either of which suggests the Graham Number test cannot be satisfied with any margin of safety. A genuine value investor requires demonstrated earning power across 3–5 years, and no such evidence is provided here.

This is a micro-cap (INR 71.7 Cr) aesthetic cosmetics company incorporated in 2013 — precisely the type of speculative, fashion-dependent enterprise I caution against in The Intelligent Investor. There is no dividend track record in the data, no current ratio, no debt metrics, and no multi-year earnings consistency. Mr. Market may be offering this at 11.90x, but when the underlying business earns 0.34% on equity, the price is not the problem — the business is. I would require the stock to trade well below tangible book with demonstrable, stable earnings before considering it. Avoid.
